title: Hydrodynamics of perfect fluids with anomalies from the fermionic path integral
abstract: The path integral of the Dirac fermion with vector and axial gauge backgrounds is analyzed near the infrared limit in the presence of residual irrelevant current-current interaction. After integrating out fermions, a semiclassical low-energy effective action is obtained, written in terms of currents. Its expression is found to correspond to the hydrodynamic action previously proposed for perfect barotropic fluids with anomalies at zero temperature. This approach also leads to two further hydrodynamic actions to be associated, respectively, with the Weyl fermion, and the Dirac fermion having independent vector and axial currents. These actions feature four- and five-dimensional bulk-boundary terms, owing to anomaly inflow, which are identified as being the so-called transgression forms. These are generalizations of Chern--Simons forms that involve two gauge fields: the dynamical field and the background field. The path-integral argument provides a ``microscopic'' explanation for several ingredients of the action formulation of hydrodynamics that are necessary to incorporate anomalies. It also clarifies the infrared reduction required to pass from the effective field theory to a local hydrodynamic description. This reduction is implemented by considering restricted variations of the action, familiar from hydrodynamics, which at the same time lead to four-dimensional equations of motion from the five-dimensional transgression terms.
summary: This work derives the hydrodynamic action for anomalous fermionic fluids by calculating the low-energy effective action from the Dirac fermion's path integral. It successfully incorporates chiral anomalies using transgression forms derived from higher-dimensional bulk terms. The resulting framework provides a microscopic, quantum field theory justification for the necessary ingredients in anomalous hydrodynamics.
main_problem: To provide a microscopic explanation for incorporating chiral anomalies into the hydrodynamic action formulation derived from fermionic path integrals.
main_result: The effective low-energy action is shown to correspond to previously proposed anomalous hydrodynamic actions, yielding specific forms for single-fluid and two-fluid systems involving transgression forms.
method: The analysis involves integrating out Dirac fermions via the path integral method, utilizing anomaly inflow concepts (5D Chern-Simons terms), and deriving the low-energy effective action through restricted variational principles.
model_or_system: The system models a perfect fluid described by an anomalous Dirac fermion coupled to background vector and axial gauge fields. The theory is analyzed in both single-fluid and two-fluid (vector/axial) regimes.
key_observables: Hydrodynamic action ($	ext{Seff}$), transgression forms, conserved currents ($J, 	ilde{J}$), and the resulting equations of motion derived from restricted variations.
important_parameters: Zero temperature limit, residual irrelevant current-current interactions, and coupling constants related to anomaly coefficients ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The derivation assumes an infrared fluid phase where a semiclassical low-energy effective action can be obtained, requiring the use of restricted variations (gauge/diffeomorphism) to define local 4D equations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from analyzing the fermionic path integral and obtaining the initial effective action via anomaly inflow. It then details the derivation of the single-fluid and two-fluid actions, culminating in applying restricted variational principles to derive the final local 4D hydrodynamic equations of motion.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter theory (anomalous hydrodynamics), the rigorous use of path integrals, effective field theories, and symmetry constraints mirrors advanced techniques used in describing quantum many-body systems far from equilibrium.
